narrative:
Based on the information provided, the model predicts there is a 47% chance you may not pass your final year. Because this probability is well above the threshold set by the school, you are required to take additional remedial courses to support your learning and help you succeed.

The most important factor influencing this prediction is that you have previously failed a class. While most students in your situation have not experienced any past failures, having even one makes a significant difference in the model’s assessment, as it suggests you may face ongoing challenges in your studies. This history was the strongest reason for the model’s decision.

Another factor that played a role, but in your favor, is your family size. You come from a smaller family (three or fewer members), which, compared to the majority of students who have larger families, is generally associated with a slightly lower risk of failing. This aspect helped reduce your predicted risk somewhat.

Your weekly study time also contributed positively. You spend between two and five hours a week studying, which is the most common amount among your peers. This level of study time is typical and did not increase your risk.

Given these factors, the main reason for the decision is your previous academic difficulty. The remedial courses are designed to give you extra support and help you build confidence moving forward. Taking advantage of these resources, staying consistent with your study habits, and seeking help when needed will give you the best chance to succeed in your final year.
